title: Get Equal Substrings Within Budget
statement:
The strings `s` and `t` have equal length. Rewriting position `i` of `s` so it holds `t[i]` costs the absolute gap between the ASCII codes of `s[i]` and `t[i]`.

Choose a block of consecutive positions and rewrite every one of them so that this part of `s` matches the same part of `t`, spending no more than `maxCost` in total. Return the largest number of positions such a block can have, or `0` when not even one position fits the budget.
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
signature: int equalSubstring(String s, String t, int maxCost)
notes:
## Intuition

Each position has its own price, `|s[i] - t[i]|`, so the task is really: find the longest run of consecutive prices whose sum stays within `maxCost`. Trying every start and end costs O(n²). Since prices are never negative, growing a window can only raise its total and shrinking it can only lower it, so one window that slides forward is enough.

## Approach

1. Keep a window `[left, right]` and its total `cost`; start with `left = 0`, `cost = 0`, `best = 0`.
2. Move `right` across the strings and add that position's price to `cost`.
3. While `cost` is above `maxCost`, subtract the price at `left` and move `left` forward.
4. The window now fits the budget; record its length `right - left + 1` in `best` if it is larger.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abcd"`, `t = "bcdf"`, `maxCost = 3`. The prices are `1, 1, 1, 2`.

- `right = 0`: `cost = 1`, window length 1, `best = 1`.
- `right = 1`: `cost = 2`, `best = 2`.
- `right = 2`: `cost = 3`, still within budget, `best = 3`.
- `right = 3`: `cost = 5 > 3`, so drop index 0 (`cost = 4`) and index 1 (`cost = 3`); the window is `[2, 3]`, length 2.

The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `right` and `left` each move forward at most n times.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- If even one price exceeds `maxCost`, the window becomes empty (`left = right + 1`), its length is 0, and the answer can legitimately be 0.
- Compare with `cost > maxCost` (strict): a total exactly equal to the budget is allowed.
- The price is the absolute difference; forgetting `Math.abs` lets negative gaps cancel positive ones.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the current window |
| `cost` | total price of rewriting the window |
| `best` | longest window that fit the budget so far |

narration.3: Nothing is inside the window yet, so it costs nothing.
narration.4: No valid window has been measured yet.
narration.6: Extend the window one position to the right each step.
narration.7: Add the price of rewriting s[right] into t[right].
narration.8: While the window costs more than the budget, it must shrink.
narration.9: Remove the price of the leftmost position from the total.
narration.10: Move the left edge one step forward.
narration.12: The window now fits the budget; keep its length if it is the longest so far.
